battle.name: 項梁起兵反秦
battle.brief: 公元前209年秦二世元年，陳勝吳廣在大澤鄉舉事，張楚號召天下；項梁與項羽於同年秋在江東吳中聚鄉民為兵，渡江西進，隸屬張楚，節節擊破秦郡兵，逼到滎陽、陳留。卡面這件斯巴達長矛是希臘重裝步兵方陣的長兵，相隔近六百年而不在江東戰場；楚軍所恃是水戰慣用的戈與徒手持矛，義兵多無重甲。

kit.name: 斯巴達長矛
kit.history: 兩米長的木槍，槍尾帶銅套。方陣裡它比劍更早決定誰站得住。

countries: 公元前209年秦二世元年秋，泗水流域的戍卒在大澤鄉舉事，秦朝在兩三個月內同時面對數支互不隸屬的反秦軍。反秦一方可以分出三層：最內層是陳勝、吳廣攻下陳縣後建立的張楚，陳勝自為將軍、吳廣為假將軍，其後稱楚王、國號張楚，設校尉、將軍、卿、相等官署，並向各地派遣偏將略地；中層是楚地舊族與鄉民自發響應的義軍，項梁、項羽起兵於吳中，聚集江東鄉民與漁戶為兵，渡江西進之後在名義上隸屬於陳勝的張楚；最外層是趙、齊、燕、魏舊地的守令與豪強各自復國、各自立王，彼此之間沒有統屬，也沒有共同作戰的約定。秦朝一方仍是郡縣制下的官僚國家：皇帝之下設丞相、廷尉、太尉與九卿，地方置郡守、縣令，軍隊以郡縣徵發的材官、騎士、車兵三種為主，關中另留常備郡兵，刑徒則用於運糧、築城與營造。中央由二世胡亥與趙高控制，章邯以少府之職奉命領兵出討。這場戰爭的交戰方並非兩個國家，而是同一個帝國之內正在崩解的秩序與正在成形的諸侯聯盟；項梁的義軍既不缺人，也不缺地名，唯獨缺統一的名分與指揮。
countriesEn: In the autumn of the first year of the Second Emperor, 209 BC, conscripts in the Sishui basin rose at Daze Village, and within two or three months the Qin dynasty was facing several armed rising armies that were subordinate to one another. The insurgents can be read in three layers. The innermost is Zhangchu, the state proclaimed by Chen Sheng and Wu Guang after they took the city of Chen: Chen Sheng appointed himself general and Wu Guang acting general, and later took the title of King of Chu under the state name of Zhangchu, with offices of commandant, general, minister and chancellor set up and envoys sent out to bring the districts under their authority. The middle layer is the volunteer bands raised in the old lands of Chu by local clans and villagers: Xiang Liang and Xiang Yu rose in the Wu region, gathered the villagers and fishermen of Jiangdong into an army, and after crossing the Yangtze placed themselves under Chen Sheng's Zhangchu in name. The outermost layer is the commandery officials and magnates of Zhao, Qi, Yan and Wei, each restoring a state and a king of their own, with no allegiance to any of the others and no agreed plan of joint action. The Qin side was still a bureaucratic state built on the commandery and county system: under the emperor stood the chancellor, the censor, the grand commandant and the Nine Offices; the provinces were governed by commandery governors and the counties by magistrates; the troops came from the craftsmen-infantry, the cavalry and the chariotry levied by the commanderies, with a standing garrison in Guanzhong and penal labourers set to hauling grain, raising works and building camps. At the centre the Second Emperor Hu Hai and Zhao Gao held control, and Zhang Han, the director of the imperial workshops, was sent out with Qin troops to put down the revolt. What is worth noting is that this was not a war between two states: it was the disintegration of an imperial order meeting a coalition of new claimants taking shape inside it. The army of Xiang Liang lacked neither men nor place names; what it lacked was a common title and a common command.
people: 項梁出自楚國項氏，世代在楚國為將，與名將項燕同族；秦滅楚之後他避居江東吳中，靠當地豪強與舊屬聚起人望。史記載他曾因獄事繫於櫟陽，請獄掾曹咎寫信給櫟陽司馬欣、以舊案情由得免，可見他在楚地官府與民間都還有未斷的人脈；他交遊的吳中子弟與舊部，成了日後起兵的班底。項羽是項梁之姪，下相人，字羽，史記稱其身長八尺餘、力能扛鼎，少年時隨叔父習兵，叔父起兵之後自任衝陣先鋒。陳勝、吳廣是這場戰爭的起火者：兩人在大澤鄉舉事，陳勝事後說出「王侯將相寧為種乎」一句話，把流民、刑徒與亡國者的怨恨變成公開的政治主張；張楚的官爵、符信與將吏任命，替各地義軍提供了可以追隨的名分。對面的關鍵人物是秦廷的二世胡亥與趙高：前者誅諸兄十二人、殉葬公主，後者隱瞞沙丘之謀而專斷朝政，使郡縣守令既得不到可信的命令，也不敢擅自出兵勤王；實際上前線的秦軍主將是少府章邯，他以郡兵、刑徒與新募之眾平定張楚主力，逼得陳勝、吳廣相殘，卻在江東西進的楚軍面前連失陳留一線，最後死於夜襲的並非秦將，而是項梁自己。
peopleEn: Xiang Liang came from the Xiang clan of Chu, which had served the state as generals for generations and belonged to the same line as the famous general Xiang Yan; after Qin destroyed Chu he withdrew to the Wu region of Jiangdong, where he gathered standing among the local magnates and old retainers. The Shiji records that he was once held in custody at Liyang on a legal matter and was released through a letter written by the prison officer Cao Jiu to the magistrate of Liyang, on the strength of precedents in an old case, which shows that his connections in the offices and the villages of Chu had not been cut; the sons of Wu and the old retainers around him became the cadre of the rising. Xiang Yu was his nephew, a man of Xiapiang, courtesy name Yu; the Shiji says he stood more than eight chi in height and could lift a ding, and in his youth he trained in arms under his uncle, taking on the part of shock troops when the uncle rose. Chen Sheng and Wu Guang were the ones who lit the fire: their rising at Daze Village produced the sentence 'Would a lord, a marquis, a general or a minister be content to remain a farmer?', which turned the resentment of conscripts, penal labourers and the dispossessed into an open political claim, and the offices, tallies and appointments of Zhangchu gave the local bands a title to rally under. On the Qin side the decisive names were the Second Emperor Hu Hai and Zhao Gao: the former killed twelve of his brothers and buried princesses with the dead, the latter concealed the business at the mound and monopolised the court, so that governors and magistrates could neither obtain a credible order nor dare to send troops to the capital on their own initiative. The man actually holding the front was Zhang Han, who took the Qin army, penal labourers and fresh levies out against the main body of Zhangchu, forced Chen Sheng and Wu Guang into the quarrels that destroyed them, and then lost the Chenliu line to the Chu army advancing out of Jiangdong; the man who fell to a night attack was not a Qin general but Xiang Liang himself.
kits: 卡面這件斯巴達長矛是希臘重裝步兵的長兵：兩米上下的木桿，前端裝青銅矛頭，尾端套著銅套，這樣的長度與重量迫使它必須雙手握持，在方陣中以整列同步推進，靠矛尖的連續指向與盾牌的互相掩護，把每一名戰士壓進一個整體。斯巴達的這套體系並非憑空而成，它依附於城邦公民制度：成年男性公民全體服兵役，經過長期體能與操練的訓練，戰時以縱深十餘列的密集方陣正面壓上，矛與盾的配合才是這件武器真正的用法。與之相較，前209年楚地的戰爭完全是另一套技術。楚軍與江東義兵所持以戈為主，長柄的矛與短兵相配合：吳越水網密布，舟師慣於以戈鈎刺，步下者則以矛、劍應敵；甲胄極不齊備，鄉民義兵多只有布衣與木杆的矛，連像樣的盾都沒有，遇上秦軍的弩矢便成片倒退。秦軍的裝備則規整得多：車兵、騎士、材官三軍齊備，蹶張弩與機弩是步兵的主要殺傷手段，戟、矛、劍、盾俱全，關中郡兵還備有雲梯、縣石與望樓一類攻城器械，並以刑徒搬運糧食、修築營壘。江東的舟船是義兵最實際的優勢：項梁軍可憑民船沿江轉運兵員與糧秣，不必依賴北方那種車隊與棧道。但方陣式長矛的制度前提在楚地完全不存在——鄉民兵沒有長期操練，編組與指揮依靠血緣與鄉誼，兵器則來自各家的舊物。兩相比較，兵器的差距只是表層，真正決定戰局的，是有沒有把個人編成可以同步行動的集體。
kitsEn: The item on this card, the Spartan dory, is the long weapon of the Greek hoplite: a wooden shaft of about two metres with a bronze head at the front and a bronze butt-spike at the rear, a length and weight that force it to be gripped with both hands and advanced in step by a whole rank, its continuous line of points and the mutual covering of shields compressing each individual fighter into a single mass. The Spartan system was not built out of nothing: it rested on the institutions of the polis, where every adult male citizen owed military service and passed through years of physical and drill training, and where in battle the phalanx closed up in ranks more than ten deep, pressed forward with spear and shield working together. That is what the weapon was really for. The war of 209 BC in the lands of Chu belonged to a completely different technology. The Chu army and the Jiangdong volunteers fought with dagger-axes above all, combining the long shaft of the spear with close weapons: the waterways of Wu and Yue made boat troops natural, and they were used to hooking with the dagger-axe, while men on foot met the enemy with spears and swords. Armour was badly uneven, and the village levies wore cloth and carried shafts of wood with a point of metal, few possessed even a serviceable shield, and they gave ground in whole lines when the Qin crossbow bolts came in. The Qin forces were far better regulated: chariots, cavalry and craftsmen-infantry were all present, the large drawn crossbow and the mechanism crossbow were the infantry's main killers, halberd, spear, sword and shield were all in service, and the Guanzhong garrisons had ladders, stone-throwers and observation towers for sieges, with penal labourers hauling grain and raising camps. The boats of Jiangdong were the volunteers' real advantage: Xiang Liang's army could move men and grain by water along the river instead of relying on wagon trains and plank roads as in the north. But the institutional precondition of a phalanx of long spears simply did not exist in Chu: the village troops had no drill, the regiments were held together by kinship and village acquaintance, and the weapons were whatever each household owned. Comparing the two, the gap in weapons was only the surface of things; what decided the fighting was whether individual soldiers could be organised into a body that moved as one.
tactics: 項梁在吳中起兵，第一個戰法是快：秦郡兵分佈於各縣，徵發與集結需要時間，項氏舊屬一呼，江東鄉民與漁戶應者立集，義軍在郡兵完成調度之前就攻破沿江縣邑，取其兵器、糧食與舟船，把臨時聚來的民眾變成有補給的軍隊。第二個戰法是水陸並進：吳中的水網使舟船成為運兵與運糧的骨幹，軍隊沿江北上再轉入陸路，避開秦軍在泗水、汝水沿線設防的重點。第三個戰法是各打各的：秦廷要求郡兵協同，但命令從關中傳到一個縣往往需要數十日，項梁不必求全滅敵軍，只要在每一處局部形成人數與士氣的優勢，逐縣拔除，這也是鄉民兵後來能逼近滎陽的原因。第四個戰法是攻守之分的清醒：滎陽秦軍據城而守，楚軍沒有雲梯、縣石這類攻城重器，強攻自然無效，糧道一拉長便難以為繼，於是在陳留一線擊潰秦廷的追擊部隊之後，實際上已到極限。第五個戰法本該是警戒，卻敗在這裡：屯兵廣武的楚軍營壘鬆散，連營未及加固、夜間巡哨不足，秦軍乘夜襲營，項梁陣亡，餘部由項羽收拾退回江南。楚漢相爭中後來屢屢重演同一個教訓：糧道、營壘與警戒，才是決定一支軍隊能走多遠的三樣東西。
tacticsEn: The first method Xiang Liang used in the Wu region was speed. The Qin county troops were scattered among the commanderies, and levying and mustering took time; at the call of the old Xiang retainers the villagers and fishermen of Jiangdong answered at once, and before the county troops had completed their concentration the volunteers broke the riverside counties, seized their weapons, grain and boats, and turned a crowd of peasants into an army with supply. The second method was to move by water and by land together: the web of waterways in Wu made boats the backbone of transport, the army went north along the river and then turned inland, avoiding the points where the Qin had concentrated along the Sishui and the Ru. The third method was to fight each battle separately. The Qin court demanded cooperation between county troops, but an order from Guanzhong needed dozens of days to reach a single county, so Xiang Liang did not need to destroy the enemy in the field; he only had to win each local engagement in numbers and in morale and take the counties one by one, and that is how troops of villagers came to sit before Xingyang. The fourth method was a clear head about attack and defence. The Qin garrison at Xingyang held the town, the Chu army had no ladders or stone-throwers for a siege, a frontal assault was hopeless, and once the grain road was stretched out the army could no longer be fed; after breaking the Qin pursuit on the Chenliu line the Chu army had in fact reached its limit. The fifth method should have been vigilance, and that is where it failed: the camp of the Chu army at Guangwu was loosely laid out, the lines were not reinforced, night watches were thin, the Qin army attacked the camp by night, Xiang Liang was killed, and the remnants were taken in hand by Xiang Yu and withdrawn south of the river. The same lesson recurs throughout the Chu-Han war: the grain road, the camp and the watch are the three things that decide how far an army can go.
data: 可以站得住的數字不多。陳勝、吳廣在大澤鄉起兵時所部為九百名戍卒；一路收兵，到達陳縣時《史記》記為車六七百乘、騎千餘、卒數萬人，攻下陳後建立張楚，其後遣將徇地時所報的兵力與據地數目顯然有誇張，參考時須打折。項梁自己的兵數史無確載，只能說江東義軍以鄉民為主，起義初期在數千至數萬之間波動，史料更強調其「素無訓練」與多為漁人鄉民，而非編制數字。地理與行程可以估算：吳中（今江蘇蘇州一帶）至滎陽（今河南滎陽）直線約七百八十公里，古代軍隊日行三四十里，折合每日十五至二十公里，若全靠陸路需四十日上下；項梁軍實際以舟車並行，又在沿江多處徵集糧秣，才可能在兩三個月內完成推進。秦軍方面的常備編制可由制度反推：郡縣可徵發材官、騎士、車兵三種，蹶張弩由士卒以腰力張臂，機弩則預儲機括，單兵可反覆射擊；秦廷還有刑徒可用於運糧與築城。楚軍攻滎陽不下、糧盡而退，以及項梁死於夜襲、楚軍退回江南，都說明任何一支靠臨時徵集起家的軍隊，在攻城器械與糧秣供應上都敵不過體制完整的國家軍。
dataEn: Few figures can be stood upon. Chen Sheng and Wu Guang rose at Daze Village with nine hundred conscripts; gathering men on the march, they reached the city of Chen with what the Shiji records as six or seven hundred carts, over a thousand horsemen and tens of thousands of foot, and after taking the city they established Zhangchu, and the numbers of men and of districts claimed by the envoys they sent out afterwards are plainly exaggerated and must be discounted. No exact figure survives for Xiang Liang's own army; it can only be said that the Jiangdong volunteers were villagers in the main, fluctuating between several thousand and some tens of thousands in the early weeks, and the sources stress their lack of drill and their character as fishermen and peasants rather than any order of battle. Distance and pace can be estimated: from Wuzhong, in the region of modern Suzhou, to Xingyang, in modern Henan, the straight line is about seven hundred and eighty kilometres; an ancient army covering thirty or forty li a day, that is fifteen to twenty kilometres, would need something like forty days on the road, and Xiang Liang's force, moving by boat and cart together and drawing grain at several points along the river, may have completed the advance in two or three months. The size of the Qin army can be inferred from the system: the commanderies could levy craftsmen-infantry, cavalry and chariotry, the large drawn crossbow was worked by the soldier's own strength while the mechanism crossbow stored its power, allowing a single man to shoot again and again, and the Qin court still had penal labourers to haul grain and raise works. The Chu failure to take Xingyang, the loss of grain that sent the army back, and Xiang Liang's death in a night attack that drove the Chu force south of the river all show the same thing: an army raised by temporary levy could not match a state army in siege equipment and in the supply of grain.
cause: 秦末的起事不是出於一時的激憤，而是四層原因疊加。第一層是徭役與兵役：秦始皇北擊匈奴、南取百越，續修阿房宮與驪山陵，徵發民力常以「丁」計，男子十六歲以上皆傅軍籍，戌邊與轉輸之役循環不息；秦廷對六國舊地尤其防范，陳勝、吳廣所屬的戍卒正是被派往泗水一線戍守的一批人，遇上大雨阻道即誤期，按律當斬，於是「王侯將相寧為種乎」一句話就足以讓九百人同時拔刀。第二層是刑罰：秦法嚴苛，什伍連坐，刑徒動以數十萬計，驪山工地與徵發路上的死者不計其數，民間對秦廷的恐懼與怨恨已累積到不需要動員的程度。第三層是六國的記憶：楚地亡國不過十餘年，項氏世代為楚將，民間對楚的認同遠未被秦的郡縣官僚取代，因此項梁一呼，江東與淮南隨即響應。第四層是中央的失序：二世誅諸兄十二人、殉葬公主，趙高專權而無人能制，地方守令各求自保，郡兵彼此不相屬，朝廷的號令出了關中便失去約束力。項梁選在陳勝之後起兵、聽命於張楚而不急於自立為王，正是出於對這份名分的依賴。
causeEn: The rising at the end of Qin was not a single burst of temper but four causes piled one on another. The first was corvée and conscription: the First Emperor had driven armies north against the Xiongnu and south into Baiyue, the work on the Epang Palace and on the mausoleum at Lishan continued, and the labour of the people was counted in ding, with every man above sixteen years of age entered on the military rolls; the duty of garrisoning the frontier and of transport came round without end, and the Qin court was at its most suspicious in the old lands of the six states. The conscripts to whom Chen Sheng and Wu Guang belonged were among those sent to hold the Sishui line; a heavy rain blocked the road, they missed their reporting date, and under the law that was punishable by death, so the words 'Would a lord, a marquis, a general or a minister be content to remain a farmer?' were enough to make nine hundred men draw their blades at once. The second cause was punishment: Qin law was severe, households were grouped for collective liability, penal labourers were counted by the hundred thousand, and deaths on the Lishan works and on the roads were beyond counting; the fear and resentment of the Qin court had grown to the point where no persuasion was needed. The third was the memory of the six states: Chu had been destroyed little more than a decade earlier, the Xiang clan had served Chu as generals for generations, and the identification of the people of Chu with the old kingdom had by no means been replaced by the Qin commandery bureaucracy, so when Xiang Liang called, Jiangdong and the lands south of the Huai answered at once. The fourth was the disorder of the centre: the Second Emperor killed twelve of his brothers and buried princesses with the dead, Zhao Gao monopolised power with no one able to restrain him, and local officials thought only of their own survival; the county troops did not belong to one another, and once the court's orders left Guanzhong they lost all power to bind. That Xiang Liang rose after Chen Sheng, and acknowledged Zhangchu instead of hastening to call himself king, was itself a sign of how much he depended on that borrowed legitimacy.
impact: 這場戰爭的直接影響有兩層。對秦朝而言，江東楚軍的西進把秦廷的兵力從北線與南線抽走，使秦軍無法集中對付任何一路；楚軍逼近滎陽、陳留之時，秦廷不得不把原本用於鎮壓張楚的郡兵回調，兵力的往返調度正是秦朝崩潰的直接機制。對楚地而言，項梁一死，楚軍退回江南，項羽收拾殘部、收攏兵權，前208年眾將迎立楚懷王孫熊心為楚王，以項梁為上將軍、項羽為武安侯，隨後項梁戰歿，項羽獨領楚軍；於是「楚」這個先由陳勝、吳廣提出、又先由他們失去的號召，最終落到項羽手上，楚漢對抗的基本格局也隨之而定。更深一層的影響在制度上：秦的郡縣徵發制與希臘的公民兵制在這十年間同時走到盡頭，一個靠刑徒與軍功維持，一個靠城邦的公民義務維持，而楚地義兵兩樣都沒有，最後靠個人統率與敵軍內部崩潰補償。戰爭留下的物質後果同樣沉重：江東的舟船被大量徵用，沿江縣邑的倉廩為軍隊取空，陳留、滎陽一線的反覆攻掠使中原的糧食生產再遭重創，漢廷日後的輸轉、屯田與徙民政策，多半是為了收拾這段留下的空缺。
impactEn: This war had two layers of direct effect. For Qin, the westward march of the Chu army from Jiangdong pulled Qin troops away from the northern and southern fronts, so that the Qin army could not concentrate against any one of them; when the Chu troops reached Xingyang and the Chenliu line, the court had to recall the county troops that had been committed against Zhangchu, and this shuttling of troops between fronts was the immediate mechanism of the dynasty's collapse. For the lands of Chu, the death of Xiang Liang sent the Chu army back south of the river, and Xiang Yu gathered the remnants and took the command; in 208 BC the generals installed King Huai's grandson Xin as King of Chu, made Xiang Liang the senior general and Xiang Yu the Lord of Wuan, and after Xiang Liang was killed Xiang Yu held the Chu army alone. Thus the claim of 'Chu' first raised by Chen Sheng and Wu Guang, and then lost by them, ended up in the hands of Xiang Yu, and with it the basic shape of the Chu-Han contest was fixed. Deeper still lies the institutional lesson: the Qin system of levying by commandery and the Greek system of citizen service both reached their end within the same decade, one sustained by penal labourers and by reward for military merit, the other by the civic duty of the polis, while the volunteers of Chu had neither, and were compensated at last by personal command and by the collapse of the enemy. The material consequences were heavy as well: the boats of Jiangdong were requisitioned in bulk, the granaries of the riverside counties were emptied for the armies, and the repeated storming of the Chenliu and Xingyang line left the grain production of the central plain broken a second time; the transport, garrison farming and resettlement policies of the Han court afterwards were largely a matter of repairing the gaps left here.
result: 結果分四層。就項梁本人而言，起兵是成功的：江東各縣響應迅速，義軍渡江之後節節擊破秦郡兵，一度逼到滎陽、陳留，在陳留一線擊潰秦廷的追擊部隊與守軍（史書對秦將秦嘉兵敗之地記載略有出入），把秦廷的平叛重心從北方拉回中原；秦二世對此的處置是加罪於郡守與將吏，於是前方更缺糧草、後方更少援兵，前線與後方的崩解同時加速。但起兵也在最高點戛然而止：屯兵廣武的楚軍營壘鬆懈，秦軍乘夜襲營，項梁陣亡，項羽收攏餘部退回江南；張楚政權在陳勝、吳廣相殘中先行瓦解，陳勝被自己的車夫所殺，吳廣與諸將各自割據，六國舊地也各自復國，楚地義軍在很長時間裡並無真正的主腦。就全局而言，這場戰爭把秦朝從主動平叛拖入被動應戰：前207年楚軍於巨鹿殲滅秦軍主力，前206年沛公入關、子嬰素車白馬出降，秦朝至此終結，楚漢爭霸隨即開打。對卡面這件斯巴達長矛而言，這場戰爭幾乎與它無關——它不曾出現在吳中、滎陽或廣武的任何一處戰場——但它是一塊很好的對照石：同一個時代裡，希臘世界靠城邦制度造出能同步推進的密集方陣，而楚地義兵靠臨時徵集與鄉誼維持數量，兩者都靠制度而非器械取勝；秦的郡縣體制同樣是一種制度，只是它把最嚴密的編制，安放在最缺少認同的兵員身上。
resultEn: The result can be read on four levels. For Xiang Liang himself the rising was a success: the counties of Jiangdong answered quickly, the volunteers broke the Qin county troops in succession after crossing the river, drove to the doors of Xingyang and Chenliu, and on the Chenliu line broke the Qin pursuit and the garrison, drawing the weight of the court's suppression from the north back into the central plain; the Second Emperor's answer was to punish the governors and generals, so that the front got less grain and the rear fewer reinforcements, and the collapse of front and rear happened at the same time. But the rising also stopped at its highest point: the Chu camp at Guangwu was sloppily laid, the Qin army attacked by night, Xiang Liang was killed, and Xiang Yu gathered what was left and withdrew south of the river. The Zhangchu state had already come apart in the quarrels between Chen Sheng and Wu Guang, with Chen Sheng killed by his own carter and Wu Guang and the other generals ruling separate districts; the old lands of the six states restored themselves one by one, and for a long time the insurgents of Chu had no real head. As to the war as a whole, it dragged Qin from the offensive into a defensive posture: in 207 BC the Chu army destroyed the Qin main force at Julu, in 206 BC the Lord of Pei entered the passes and the Crown Prince Ying came out in a plain carriage with white horses, and the dynasty ended, opening the Chu-Han struggle that followed. As for the Spartan dory on this card, the war had almost nothing to do with it: it never appeared on any battlefield at Wuzhong, at Xingyang or at Guangwu. It is useful rather as a control. In the same age, the Greek world built a phalanx that could advance in step through the institutions of the polis, while the volunteers of Chu maintained their numbers by temporary levy and by village acquaintance; both won through institutions rather than through weapons, and the Qin commandery system was an institution too, only one that set the tightest order upon soldiers who had the least share in it.
